weekly_focus.headline: Stability-first fueling to rebuild energy and support performance
weekly_focus.context: Early menstrual phase with morning training and light baseline stress. Food this week works best when it supports steady energy, recovery, and focus rather than optimisation.

emphasise.why: Consistent intake often stabilises energy and reduces stress load during cycle recovery.
Protein anchoring tends to support training recovery, satiety, and cognitive clarity.
Adequate carbs usually improve performance tolerance and reduce perceived effort, especially with morning sessions.
Regular fat intake supports hormonal signalling and helps meals feel more complete.

de_emphasise.why: Extended gaps can increase fatigue and amplify cravings later in the day.
Meals lacking balance often lead to low energy and reduced training quality.
Extra decision-making can add stress without improving outcomes this week.

training_recovery_support.nutrition_cue: Energy often feels more stable when there is some fuel support before or soon after training.
Sessions usually feel better when meals earlier in the day include enough carbohydrates and protein.
Recovery tends to improve when meals remain regular rather than becoming lighter or skipped.

physiological_signals.what_it_may_indicate: Often reflects higher energy demand during cycle recovery rather than poor food choices.

physiological_signals.signal: Flat or sluggish energy in training
physiological_signals.what_it_may_indicate: May suggest earlier meals were too light or delayed.

physiological_signals.what_itay_indicate: Nutrition timing and balance are likely well aligned with training and recovery.
